newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - IVAN WONG COMMENTS ON MALAYSIAN PALM OIL.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - IVAN WONG COMMENTS ON MALAYSIAN PALM OIL.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 - The palm crop in July turned out the way we had expected. However, because of a drop in the OER, CPO production rose marginally less than our previous estimate. It rose 35,000 tonnes or 4.5 percent to an estimated 823,000 tonnes. Compared to July last year, production expanded nearly 14 percent. Growth in the 7 months to July was around 11 percent. In August-September growth is likely to decelerate to 4 percent. Similarly the month-on-month seasonal rise in production is also expected to be not more than 5 percent.

In contrast to the modest rise in production, the increase in offtake was much more vigorous than we expected. Palm oil exports surged to an estimated 705,000 tonnes in July from 612,100 tonnes a month earlier. The robust exports were boosted by a surprisingly large increase of around 80,000 tonnes to an estimated 145,000 tonnes in shipments to countries in West Asia. Egypt alone raised its offtake by some 50,000 tonnes to an estimated 68,000 tonnes. This almost equalled the previous record monthly offtake of 69,300 tonnes registered in June 1992.

The previous second largest offtake was 58,600 tonnes in July 1993. In both 1992 and 1993, the unusually large offtake was not sustained as the following month saw a marked reduction. An estimated 115,000 tonnes palm oil were shipped to Egypt in January-June, down from 174,800 tonnes and 146,000 tonnes in the same periods of 1996 and 1992. Total shipments for these 2 years were 346,900 tonnes and 324,700 tonnes respectively. The robust export number helped to moderate the seasonal rise in palm oil stocks to an estimated 805,000 tonnes at end July from 786,100 tonnes at end June.

Compared to a year earlier, stocks were higher by around 50,000 tonnes. End-July stocks of CPO were estimated at 465,000 tonnes, up from 404,700 tonnes in the preceding month and 402,700 tonnes a year ago. The healthy exports enabled refiners to run down their stocks of PPO to an estimated 340,000 tonnes from 381,400 tonnes at end June. We are maintaining our projections of a month-on-month build-up in palm oil stocks of close to 100,000 tonnes in August-October. CPO price had remained steady to firm since mid-July. Its strength was underpinned by the continued weakness of the ringgit.

In the 3 weeks ended August 1, CPO futures advanced 26-38 ringgit. The market posted further gains of 44-32 ringgit in the last 3 days on chart-biased buying activities and active covering in the cash market. While the firmness in CPO values also reflected the strong palm oil export performance in July, the export price of products in U.S. dollar terms had hardly improved. October/December RBD olein was quoted at $527.50 yesterday, down from $530 on July 14. Malaysian refiners could not raise their product price because of keen competition from Indonesia whose currency also weakened against the dollar.

Equally significant is that Indonesian CPO production is picking up strongly with industry sources reporting a high single-digit month-on-month rise in CPO output in July. Price of competing oils like SBO, RSO and sunoil also hardly moved while CNO price dropped further losing $45 to $560 CIF Rotterdam between mid-July and yesterday. Suffice to say, the currency volatility facing the 3 leading vegoil exporting countries Malaysia, Indonesia and Philippines has clouded the price outlook for their primary export commodities.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
